To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelial cells express a heterodimeric receptor for IL-13, consisting of a 65- to-75-kD subunit and the IL-4 receptor (IL-4 R) alpha chain, which mediates IL-13-induced signaling.
endothelial cell-bound IL-4 and -13 mediate VCAM-1 expression and subsequent transmigrations of eosinophiles via the IL-4 receptor and a novel IL-13 receptor, respectively.
endothelial cells express a functional IL-4 and an IL-13 receptor that does not require the common gamma-chain for signal transduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the receptor structure for IL-4/IL-13 in endothelial cells.
the characterization of the IL-4-IL-13R on endothelial cells.
the elucidation of the structure and function of the IL-4 and the IL-13 receptors on human endothelial cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endothelial cells express a functional receptor for IL- 13, which is composed of the IL-4 receptor and an additional, novel IL-13-specific binding subunit.
endothelial cells express a novel IL-13R alpha and that IL-4R, IL-13R, and their ligands are functionally interchangeable.
IL-4 and Il-13 signal through a heterodimer of IL-4R-alpha and IL-13-R, the latter being a novel protein, and that both cytokines are able to bind with high affinity to the same IL-4R complex.

the IL-4 and the IL-13 receptors on endothelial cells are composed of two subunits, the IL- 4R alpha and a novel 65- to -75-kD subunit, which is not the common gamma c.

the IL-4 and the IL-13 receptors on human endothelial do not require gamma c, the common subunit for the IL-2 receptor, and that the IL-13 receptor is distinct from that of IL-4.
